newsitem.title: USA: Missing Detroit guard found in bank basement.
newsitem.headline: Missing Detroit guard found in bank basement.

text.p: An unarmed bank security guard who disappeared during a shooting rampage was found huddled in the bank's basement 28 hours after the bloody ordeal that claimed four lives, police said Wednesday.

The guard, Virene Brown, had been missing since a man armed with a shotgun ordered her to leave a Comerica branch bank after wounding the bank's assistant manager shortly after 10 a.m. on Tuesday, according to police accounts.

Police wanted to question Brown, but do not believe she was a part of the shooting spree. Brown was found by a maintenance worker at about 2 p.m. on Wednesday, hiding behind some mechanical equipment, police and Comerica officials said. She had apparently been there since the shooting.
"How she got there or why she ended up there we don't know as yet," said Officer Allene Ray of the Detroit Police Department.

Brown, who works for Guardsmark Inc. of Memphis, Tennessee, was taken to St. John Hospital and Medical Centre. A hospital spokeswoman said Brown was diagnosed with post traumatic stress syndrome and admitted for observation. She was listed in good condition.
After first shooting a jogger in the face, Allen Griffin, 21, entered the bank on Detroit's east side, saying he intended to rob it, according to some witness accounts.

After wounding assistant manager Lisa Griffin, 38, who was not related to the gunman, the would-be robber killed two more employees -- branch office manager Stanley Pijanowski III, 52, and James Isom, 25, a retail services representative.

On his way out, Griffin grabbed 77-year-old Stanley Hays as a hostage to protect him from police, who had been alerted by a silent alarm and had the building surrounded. Moments later police killed Griffin in a nearby alley after he shot Hays to death.
Comerica spokeswoman Kathy Pitton declined to say whether Comerica had installed more security measures at its branches since the shooting, citing a policy against discussing security.
Police said on Wednesday they still had no clear motive for Griffin's actions, although they said he was reported to be depressed over a failing marriage and other domestic problems.

Lisa Griffin was listed in fair condition on Wednesday at a local hospital with a gunshot wound to the chin. The jogger, 23-year-old Eric Skalnek, remained in serious condition, said a spokeswoman for St. John Hospital and Medical Centre.
Mourners and neighbours in the working class neighbourhood where the shooting occurred put flowers and other memorials in front of the bank, which is closed while police continue their investigation.
